abortion.text: Berning says he opposes abortion and supports practical assistance for women who want to continue a pregnancy.
abortion.quote: I oppose abortion. I also believe being pro-life must mean more than telling a frightened woman what she should not do.

tax.text: He voted for the Inflation Reduction Act, which included a minimum tax on large multinational businesses and major public investments.
tax.quote: Assuring that our largest multinational businesses, some of which are paying very low or no taxes, finally pay a minimum 15% tax rate.

wages.text: He voted for the Raise the Wage Act.
wages.quote: Vote Question: On Passage Raise the Wage Act

trade.text: He introduced bills to reform the Jones Act and argued for more competition in domestic cargo shipping.
trade.quote: most of the world's shipping is by way of an international merchant marine functioning in an open, competitive market.

debt.text: His agenda says to preserve and strengthen Social Security and Medicare.
debt.quote: We must preserve and strengthen Social Security and Medicare and fulfill our commitments to our veterans and others.

housing.text: He introduced a bill to encourage affordable housing development in designated transit-oriented areas.
housing.quote: By encouraging affordable housing near existing transportation infrastructure, we can help reduce transportation costs for residents, improve access to jobs and essential services and support more efficient and sustainable community growth.

schools.text: He requested and supported federal funding that helps Hawaii public schools educate military children.
schools.quote: $70 million for Impact Aid programs, which help Hawaii’s public schools by partially reimbursing the cost of educating military children.

safety.text: He backed a funding measure that increased support for law enforcement while also funding prevention and education.
safety.quote: The more than $4.2 billion in the bill to help local and state law enforcement will help not only to investigate and prosecute crime but will also go to prevention and education programs to stop crime before it happens.

immigration.text: His agenda supports expanding legal immigration while curtailing illegal immigration.
immigration.quote: Support expanded legal immigration while curtailing illegal immigration

guns.text: He voted for the Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2021.
guns.quote: Vote Question: On Passage Bipartisan Background Checks Act

abortion.text: He called the Supreme Court decision overturning Roe v. Wade tragic and said Hawai‘i should stand against further restrictions on rights.
abortion.quote: Our Hawai‘i had it right with our first-in-the-nation law in 1970, and must now stand strong with other like-minded states against the further assault on women’s and other rights

health.text: He voted for the Inflation Reduction Act, including Medicare drug-price negotiation and expanded Affordable Care Act premium subsidies.
health.quote: Empowers the federal government to negotiate drug prices on the highest cost single-source drugs purchased in Medicare, lowering prices for seniors and people with disabilities.

energy.text: He voted for the Inflation Reduction Act, which he described as making a major U.S. climate investment.
energy.quote: The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 (Act), which will make the largest climate investment in American history

voting.text: He voted for the For the People Act and other measures addressing voter access.
voting.quote: Voted YEA on H.R. 1, the For the People Act, which would address voter access, election integrity and security, campaign finance, and ethics for the three branches of government.

tax.text: He proposed taxes on empty homes and visitors to fund help with housing costs for people in need.
tax.quote: The tax would go to help the homeless and needy to pay rent or buy homes.

wages.text: He listed a living wage and universal basic income among his campaign priorities.
wages.quote: My top issues are: universal health care, non violence/anti war, housing first, expanding public education from pre K through college and/or trade school, food production and knowledge, a living wage/universal basic income, ranked choice voting, campaign finance reform, and getting the military presence off our islands and out of other countries.

trade.text: He said he supports fully repealing the Jones Act.
trade.quote: Getting rid of the Jones Act is Top 10 or so of my issues. I support a full repeal.

safety.text: He proposed changing police training or shifting some police resources to community jobs.
safety.quote: I would fight to get police trained in a more helpful way, or shrink the police force to build other community jobs focused on building society.

immigration.text: He called for a fast immigration process with a hearing before a judge and an individualized, humane decision.
immigration.quote: Do their interview and have them before a judge within a week or 2. Also with ending wars, I mean any secret invasions, coups, or any other kind of CIA/US overthrow.

health.text: He said universal health care is his top issue and that he would push for a national vote on it.
health.quote: Universal health care is my number 1 issue! I will get it passed or expose those who will not vote for it so we can vote them out

tax.text: He said he would relieve tax burdens on individuals and businesses.
tax.quote: Relieve tax burden on individuals and businesses; reform regulatory environment for businesses

debt.text: In a candidate questionnaire, he said Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid should be given back to individuals or collective entities to manage for their futures.
debt.quote: Safety nets are for emergency, exigent circumstances, not routine, regular, or even abnormal conditions. These programs need to be given back to the individuals and/or collective entities to plan, manage, invest and incentivized to prepare for their future.

tax.text: He proposes increasing the child tax credit for families.
tax.quote: Increase the child tax credit to provide greater tax relief for families.

trade.text: He says he would oppose the Jones Act's restriction on shipping competition to Hawaii.
trade.quote: anyone campaigning on affordability while refusing to challenge a law restricting shipping competition to an island state should raise red flags.

housing.text: Awa proposes using suitable federal land to create homes for local residents.
housing.quote: unlocking suitable federal land for local homes.

safety.text: Awa proposes temporarily deploying National Guard units to support local law enforcement in high-crime areas.
safety.quote: Temporary deployment of National Guard units to support local law enforcement in high crime areas identified by crime data and local requests, focused on restoring public safety.

guns.text: He voted against a bill that would have tightened Hawaii's assault-weapons restrictions.
guns.quote: Rhoads and Sens. Brandon Elefante and Joy San Buenaventura voted to pass the amended version, and Sens. Mike Gabbard and Brenton Awa voted against.

abortion.text: He voted against a bill protecting abortion patients and providers from out-of-state penalties.
abortion.quote: SB 1 passed in the Senate this week with 22 votes in support and three in opposition. Democratic Sen. Mike Gabbard and the only two Republicans, Sens. Kurt Fevella and Brenton Awa, voted no.

cannabis.text: He helped introduce a recreational-marijuana legalization bill and said he supports legalization, though not that bill's dispensary model.
cannabis.quote: Awa said that he supports legalizing recreational marijuana but not in the form proposed under SB 375.

health.text: Awa proposes expanding federally funded community health centers in Hawaii to reduce care costs.
health.quote: We can expand federally funded community health centers across Hawaii that focus on care rather than copays.

energy.text: Awa says energy policy should prioritize reliable, affordable power and not move faster than residents can afford.
energy.quote: Clean energy matters, but energy policy cannot move faster than people's ability to pay their bills.

tax.text: She opposed cutting Social Security and Medicare for solvency and backed closing tax loopholes for the wealthy to support those benefits.
tax.quote: I do not support proposals that gut Medicare and Social Security for solvency. Instead, we can close loopholes in our tax policies that have allowed the ultra-rich to avoid paying their fair share of taxes.

trade.text: She called for removing tariffs on U.S. allies, saying they raise costs for families and businesses.
trade.quote: We have to remove tariffs on our allies which have driven up the cost of food and goods, and made it difficult for businesses to survive.

debt.text: She rejected cutting Medicare and Social Security to address solvency and supported raising taxes on high earners to fund benefits.
debt.quote: I do not support proposals that gut Medicare and Social Security for solvency.

housing.text: She said housing inventory must increase and cited federal funding for affordable housing developments.
housing.quote: We must increase our housing inventory while protecting the homes we have.

schools.text: She called for universal access to quality public education and described public education funding as an investment in Hawaiʻi’s future.
schools.quote: Our families deserve universal access to free, quality public education for children of all ages.

immigration.text: She opposed expanded ICE operations and called for transparency, accountability, and humane treatment in immigration enforcement.
immigration.quote: I will not support expanded ICE operations without guaranteed transparency, true accountability, and humane treatment.

guns.text: She advocated for universal background checks, assault-weapons restrictions, and red-flag laws.
guns.quote: I’ve advocated for nationwide gun reform measures including banning assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, mandating comprehensive background checks for all gun purchases and transfers, addressing the proliferation of “ghost guns,” and implementing Red Flag Laws

abortion.text: She opposed restrictions on reproductive health care and cosponsored legislation to codify abortion access.
abortion.quote: I also cosponsored The Women’s Health Protection Act which would codify the right to abortion care

energy.text: She called for aggressive action on climate change and increased renewable energy production.
energy.quote: Aggressive action needs to be taken to address climate change impacts and increase renewable energy production.

voting.text: She supports the For the People Act and voting reforms intended to expand access.
voting.quote: I actively support crucial campaign finance reforms at the federal level, including the For the People Act and the DISCLOSE Act.
